title: Integrations: OCPP, Modbus, OCPI, roaming | VOOL
description: Connect VOOL to building management, energy management, other charging platforms and roaming networks.

sections.title: Open protocols, so the site is never locked in
sections.lead: VOOL chargers and LMCs speak the standard protocols of the industry. Use our software, someone else’s, or both.

cells: Connect VOOL chargers to another back end, or other makers’ chargers to the VOOL Portal
Mixed sites, operators with their own platform
Read measurements and set current limits on the VOOL LMC
Building management, energy management, batteries and solar
Exchange locations, sessions and prices with partner platforms
Roaming: drivers use other providers’ apps and cards at your public chargers
Plug & Charge; bidirectional charging by firmware update in Q1 2027

items.title: Chargers from several makers
items.text: Keep the chargers you have. Add them to the VOOL Portal over OCPP and manage users and billing in one place.

items.title: Building management system
items.text: The BMS reads charging load from the LMC and can lower the limit during peaks.

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text: A community integration reads VOOL devices over Modbus. Useful for home automation with solar or a battery.

items.title: Your own operator
items.text: Point the chargers to the operator’s OCPP back end. Load management keeps running locally on the LMC.

items.title: Roaming
items.text: Through Hubject, public VOOL chargers accept the charging apps and cards drivers already have. Providers are being added now.

items.title: Lithuania: DAEI
items.text: Charging data is reported for DAEI units, and you are paid for the electricity you charge.

items.q: Does load management need the internet?
items.a: No. The LMC and the chargers talk locally. The internet is needed for the app, billing and remote support.

items.q: Which earthing systems does the LMC support?
items.a: IT earthing systems, common in parts of Norway, are not supported for load management. Charging itself works normally.

items.q: How are chargers connected to the LMC?
items.a: Over CAN in a daisy chain, or over the local network.

items.q: Is Modbus write access on by default?
items.a: No. It is enabled on the LMC when you need it.

sections.title: Planning an integration?
sections.lead: Tell us what the other system is. We send the register map or the OCPP details.
